nodes.title: Implement the plan (8 steps)
nodes.goal:
Extend this job runner into a small job platform: add job priorities with fair scheduling across tenants, delayed and recurring jobs, dependencies between jobs, per-kind rate limits, webhook notifications for job state changes, and an audit log with a statistics API. Expose all of them through the REST API and the web dashboard. Follow SPEC.md.

Work through the following steps in order; each step lists its goal and files.

Step 1 of 8: Contract: job fields, records, errors, transactions, Runner method stubs [A]
This is the contract every other sub-task builds on; follow SPEC.md for names, types, and defaults, and give each new name a docstring. In jobrunner/models.py add the Job fields priority=0, tenant='default', depends_on=[] (a list of ints), definition_id=None and cancel_reason=None, all in Job.to_dict, and the dataclasses RecurringJob, RateLimit, Subscription, Notification and AuditEntry with the fields of SPEC.md and a to_dict each. In jobrunner/errors.py add NotFound(JobRunnerError) and make JobNotFound a subclass of it. In jobrunner/store.py add the complete helper JobStore.transaction(), a context manager that commits every write inside it at once at the end of the outermost block (and rolls back on an exception); every existing write method must commit only outside a transaction. In jobrunner/runner.py give Runner.submit the keyword arguments priority, tenant, run_at and depends_on with the checks of SPEC.md 'Jobs' (it may ignore their effect for now), and add every new Runner method of SPEC.md 'Public interface' with its signature, a docstring, and a runnable default: readers return empty results ([] or the stats dict with zeros), lookups of an id raise NotFound or JobNotFound, deliver_notifications returns 0, and methods that create or change records raise NotImplementedError. Do not change run_once. Write tests/test_contract.py; it checks only what stays true once the features are implemented (fields, records, to_dict, transactions, signatures), never the default bodies.
Modify: jobrunner/models.py, jobrunner/errors.py, jobrunner/store.py, jobrunner/runner.py
Tests to write: tests/test_contract.py

Step 2 of 8: Job selection: priorities, tenant rotation, dependencies, rate limits [S]
Implement everything that decides which job run_once picks, in jobrunner/runner.py and jobrunner/store.py. These three features all change the same selection in run_once, so they are one sub-task. (1) Persistence: store the new Job fields (priority, tenant, depends_on, definition_id, cancel_reason) in the jobs table (JobStore.add takes them as keyword arguments, including next_run_at for run_at and definition_id) and make submit store them. (2) Replace the in-memory heap in run_once with a selection over the stored PENDING jobs as SPEC.md 'Running jobs' says: a job can run when it is due, every dependency SUCCEEDED, and its kind is under its rate limit; among those pick the highest priority, then the tenant whose most recent start is oldest (a tenant that never started first; persist the starts so this survives a restart), then next_run_at, then id. (3) Record every start (kind, tenant, time) in SQLite for rate limits and tenant turns. (4) Dependencies (SPEC.md 'Dependencies'): submit checks depends_on; when a job becomes FAILED or CANCELLED in any code path (run_once, cancel, restart recovery) cancel its PENDING dependents downstream with cancel_reason 'dependency_failed'; a job submitted with an already failed or cancelled dependency is cancelled at once; cancel() sets cancel_reason 'cancel_requested'. (5) Implement set_priority, queue, tenants, dependents, set_rate_limit, clear_rate_limit and list_rate_limits. Write tests/test_selection.py.
Modify: jobrunner/runner.py, jobrunner/store.py
Tests to write: tests/test_selection.py

Step 3 of 8: Delayed and recurring jobs [R]
Implement SPEC.md 'Delayed and recurring jobs' in jobrunner/runner.py and jobrunner/store.py: a recurring table; schedule_recurring, get_recurring, list_recurring, update_recurring, pause_recurring, resume_recurring, delete_recurring and recurring_jobs; and at the start of run_once, before a job is picked, create the jobs of due definitions (at most one unfinished job per definition, missed periods skipped, next_run_at moved to the first period after now). Create those jobs the way submit does (JobStore.add with priority, tenant and definition_id) so they take part in selection like any other job. run_at is already handled by submit. Write tests/test_recurring_jobs.py.
Modify: jobrunner/runner.py, jobrunner/store.py
Tests to write: tests/test_recurring_jobs.py

Step 4 of 8: Webhook notifications through an outbox [N]
Implement SPEC.md 'Webhook notifications' in jobrunner/runner.py and jobrunner/store.py: subscriptions and outbox tables; subscribe, unsubscribe, list_subscriptions, list_notifications, deliver_notifications and retry_notification. Every state change listed in SPEC.md 'Audit log' (creation, start, success, retry, failure, every cancellation, restart recovery, dependency cancellations) must write one outbox row per matching subscription in the same JobStore.transaction() as the change itself: find every place in runner.py that saves a new status. Delivery: per subscription and job in order, exponential backoff 1, 2, 4, 8 s, dead after the 5th failed attempt, a BaseException from the sender propagates and leaves the row unchanged. Write tests/test_notifications.py.
Modify: jobrunner/runner.py, jobrunner/store.py
Tests to write: tests/test_notifications.py

Step 5 of 8: Audit log and statistics [H]
Implement SPEC.md 'Audit log and statistics' in jobrunner/runner.py and jobrunner/store.py: an audit_log table, one entry for every state change with the reasons of the SPEC.md table, written in the same JobStore.transaction() as the change (find every place in runner.py that saves a new status, as the outbox does); history, audit_log and stats (by_status, by_kind, by_tenant, finished, failed, failure_rate, average_attempts over the window now - window_s < time <= now). Write tests/test_audit.py.
Modify: jobrunner/runner.py, jobrunner/store.py
Tests to write: tests/test_audit.py

Step 6 of 8: REST API for every platform feature [E]
Extend jobrunner/api.py with every route of SPEC.md 'REST API': the new POST /jobs fields and all the (new) routes, calling the Runner methods. Map ValueError to 400 (also for a body that is not an object or lacks a required field, and for query values that are not numbers), NotFound to 404 and InvalidTransition to 409, with {'error': message}. The Runner methods are only stubs while you work; test the routes with a fake runner object or by checking the calls, plus the routes that already work. Write tests/test_api_platform.py.
Modify: jobrunner/api.py
Tests to write: tests/test_api_platform.py

Step 7 of 8: Dashboard pages for every platform feature [F]
Extend jobrunner/dashboard.py render_page with every (new) page of SPEC.md 'Dashboard' (/queue, /recurring, /jobs/<id>/dependencies, /rate-limits, /notifications, /jobs/<id>/history, /audit, /stats) built from the Runner methods, with exactly the titles, table classes, columns, number formats and forms SPEC.md lists, HTML-escaping all text; 404 with 'Not found' for unknown pages and ids, 400 for an invalid query. Keep render_jobs unchanged. The Runner methods are only stubs while you work; test the pages with a fake runner object. Write tests/test_dashboard_pages.py.
Modify: jobrunner/dashboard.py
Tests to write: tests/test_dashboard_pages.py

Step 8 of 8: Integration and end-to-end tests [G]
Write tests/test_platform.py exercising SPEC.md end to end through the REST API and the dashboard: a pipeline with tenants, priorities and dependencies, a rate limit next to a recurring job, webhook delivery with retries, the audit log and statistics, and a restart (a new JobStore and Runner on the same database file) that keeps every record. Fix any mismatch between the parts that these tests reveal.
Modify: jobrunner/runner.py, jobrunner/store.py, jobrunner/api.py, jobrunner/dashboard.py
Tests to write: tests/test_platform.py
